rules.summary: This specification defines what a conforming implementation MUST do; it does not prescribe a particular implementation technique unless this document explicitly makes an implementation property normative.

rules.title: The words MUST , MUST NOT , SHOULD , SHOULD NOT , and MAY are normative
rules.summary: The words MUST , MUST NOT , SHOULD , SHOULD NOT , and MAY are normative.

rules.summary: Undefined behavior is behavior for which this specification imposes no requirements. Operations expressible in safe CobaltC without entering an unsafe context MUST NOT have undefined behavior.

rules.summary: A translation unit defines exactly one module. The module declaration of a translation unit establishes the module defined by that translation unit. A translation unit MUST contain exactly one module declaration.

rules.title: Submodules are distinct modules and MUST be defined by separate translation units
rules.summary: Submodules are distinct modules and MUST be defined by separate translation units.

rules.title: A submodule is not part of its parent module merely because it is organized beneath that module in a source-fi
rules.summary: A submodule is not part of its parent module merely because it is organized beneath that module in a source-file hierarchy.

rules.title: An implementation MAY use any source-file, directory, project, or compilation-unit organization internally, pr
rules.summary: An implementation MAY use any source-file, directory, project, or compilation-unit organization internally, provided that the resulting module structure and behavior conform to this specification.

rules.title: Whitespace separates lexical tokens where necessary and otherwise has no semantic meaning. An implementation M
rules.summary: Whitespace separates lexical tokens where necessary and otherwise has no semantic meaning. An implementation MAY accept additional source encodings as extensions, but a conforming implementation MUST accept UTF-8.

rules.title: A declaration that is not exported remains available only within the access permitted by the ordinary name-res
rules.summary: A declaration that is not exported remains available only within the access permitted by the ordinary name-resolution and module rules. External code MUST NOT access a non-exported declaration merely because it knows its name or because the declaration appears in a source file belonging to the module.

rules.title: The export boundary provides an explicit software-engineering boundary: declarations that are not exported MAY
rules.summary: The export boundary provides an explicit software-engineering boundary: declarations that are not exported MAY be changed without changing the externally visible interface, provided that the specified behavior and requirements of the exported interface remain compatible.

rules.title: An implementation MAY provide additional visibility mechanisms as extensions, but such mechanisms MUST be dist
rules.summary: An implementation MAY provide additional visibility mechanisms as extensions, but such mechanisms MUST be distinguishable from standard CobaltC behavior and MUST NOT silently alter the semantics of a valid CobaltC 1.0.3 program.

rules.title: Reserved literals have fixed language-defined meanings and MUST NOT be declared as user-defined identifiers or
rules.summary: Reserved literals have fixed language-defined meanings and MUST NOT be declared as user-defined identifiers or shadowed by an inner declaration.

rules.title: Reserved keywords, reserved literals, and reserved predefined type names are collectively referred to as prote
rules.summary: Reserved keywords, reserved literals, and reserved predefined type names are collectively referred to as protected names . Protected names MUST NOT be declared as user-defined identifiers or shadowed by an inner declaration.

rules.title: Identifiers MUST NOT contain prohibited format or directional-control characters
rules.location: 6. Identifiers — Identifier Security and Unicode Restrictions [L368-L371]

rules.location: 6. Identifiers — Identifier Security and Unicode Restrictions [L368-L371]
rules.summary: An identifier that violates the requirements of Appendix B is a compile-time error.

rules.summary: A floating-point literal MUST contain either a decimal point or an exponent.

rules.summary: A floating-point literal MUST contain at least one decimal digit before an exponent, and an exponent MUST contain at least one decimal digit.

rules.summary: Integer literals MAY be typed from context where possible; without a contextual integer type, the implementation uses i32 when the value is representable and MUST otherwise require an explicit type.

rules.title: A literal whose value cannot be represented by its required type is a compile-time error
rules.summary: A literal whose value cannot be represented by its required type is a compile-time error.

rules.summary: A module establishes a namespace. A translation unit MUST contain exactly one module declaration.

rules.title: Imports do not implicitly re-export declarations
rules.summary: Imports do not implicitly re-export declarations.

rules.summary: An export MUST always be specified within an export { ... } block.

rules.summary: Unlike import declarations, a standalone export declaration, such as export someType; MUST NOT occur.

rules.summary: Any declaration not listed in the module's export { ... } block is module-local and MUST NOT be externally accessible.

rules.summary: Two translation units MUST NOT define the same module for one program. Circular module dependencies MAY be supported, but name resolution MUST remain well-defined; an unresolved dependency is a compile-time error.

rules.title: Inner declarations MAY shadow outer declarations where permitted
rules.summary: Inner declarations MAY shadow outer declarations where permitted.

rules.title: A constant initializer MUST satisfy the implementation's constant-expression requirements, and an implementati
rules.summary: A constant initializer MUST satisfy the implementation's constant-expression requirements, and an implementation MUST document those requirements.

rules.title: Integer overflow, division by zero, and invalid shift operations are not silently memory-unsafe. An implementa
rules.summary: Integer overflow, division by zero, and invalid shift operations are not silently memory-unsafe. An implementation MUST diagnose statically provable invalid constant operations and MUST otherwise apply the failure semantics specified by Section 27.

rules.title: A raw pointer value MAY represent an address that is null, invalid, dangling, or otherwise refer to memory tha
rules.summary: A raw pointer value MAY represent an address that is null, invalid, dangling, or otherwise refer to memory that is not currently a valid value of type T .

rules.title: The language does not automatically establish the validity or lifetime of a raw pointer
rules.summary: The language does not automatically establish the validity or lifetime of a raw pointer.

rules.title: A raw pointer MUST NOT be used to bypass the ownership or borrowing rules of safe CobaltC code
rules.summary: A raw pointer MUST NOT be used to bypass the ownership or borrowing rules of safe CobaltC code.

rules.title: Code that uses raw pointers to access managed memory is responsible for maintaining the validity, lifetime, al
rules.summary: Code that uses raw pointers to access managed memory is responsible for maintaining the validity, lifetime, alignment, and aliasing requirements of the accessed value.

rules.title: The compiler MUST NOT infer ownership, borrowing, or lifetime guarantees from the existence of a raw pointer
rules.summary: The compiler MUST NOT infer ownership, borrowing, or lifetime guarantees from the existence of a raw pointer.

rules.title: The compiler MUST reject any operation that would mutate a value through a shared managed pointer or otherwise
rules.summary: The compiler MUST reject any operation that would mutate a value through a shared managed pointer or otherwise violate the exclusivity requirements of a mutable managed pointer.

rules.title: Assignments, function arguments, and return values MUST have compatible types
rules.summary: Assignments, function arguments, and return values MUST have compatible types.

rules.title: A mutable managed pointer MAY be used where a shared managed pointer is required, subject to borrowing and lif
rules.summary: A mutable managed pointer MAY be used where a shared managed pointer is required, subject to borrowing and lifetime rules.

rules.summary: This represents a shared reborrow and temporarily suspends conflicting mutable use.

rules.title: Implicit conversions MUST NOT silently remove nullability, create ownership, destroy ownership, increase acces
rules.summary: Implicit conversions MUST NOT silently remove nullability, create ownership, destroy ownership, increase access capability, invalidate a lifetime guarantee, or perform unsafe reinterpretation.

rules.title: An explicit conversion MAY be provided, but an explicit conversion MUST NOT be a mechanism for bypassing the o
rules.summary: An explicit conversion MAY be provided, but an explicit conversion MUST NOT be a mechanism for bypassing the ownership, borrowing, lifetime, or safety rules of safe CobaltC.

rules.title: Inference MUST preserve ownership, binding mutability, managed-pointer access capability, nullability, borrowi
rules.summary: Inference MUST preserve ownership, binding mutability, managed-pointer access capability, nullability, borrowing, and lifetime distinctions.

rules.title: A shared borrow infers T* ; a mutable borrow infers mut T* . Inference MUST NOT infer mutable access from shar
rules.summary: A shared borrow infers T* ; a mutable borrow infers mut T* . Inference MUST NOT infer mutable access from shared access alone.

rules.summary: When no unique type can be established, the implementation MUST require an explicit type rather than choose an arbitrary type.

rules.summary: The compiler MAY implement inference using regions, constraints, control-flow analysis, graphs, or another sound technique.

rules.summary: Those techniques are not additional source syntax.

rules.title: A generic declaration MUST NOT rely on properties of a type argument that are not established by the declarati
rules.summary: A generic declaration MUST NOT rely on properties of a type argument that are not established by the declaration's constraints or by the ordinary rules of the language.

rules.title: Exporting a type makes the type name available to external code but MUST NOT, by itself, make the representati
rules.summary: Exporting a type makes the type name available to external code but MUST NOT, by itself, make the representation of that type available to external code.

rules.title: External code MAY name an exported type, use the type in function signatures, and pass or return values or man
rules.summary: External code MAY name an exported type, use the type in function signatures, and pass or return values or managed pointers to the type, subject to the ordinary rules of the type system.

rules.title: External code MUST NOT directly inspect, access, or manipulate the representation of an exported type unless t
rules.summary: External code MUST NOT directly inspect, access, or manipulate the representation of an exported type unless that representation is explicitly exposed by a language mechanism defined by this specification.

rules.title: In particular, external code MUST NOT access fields, layout, or other representation details solely because th
rules.summary: In particular, external code MUST NOT access fields, layout, or other representation details solely because the type is exported.

rules.title: An exported type MAY therefore be used as an opaque type by external code while remaining fully defined within
rules.summary: An exported type MAY therefore be used as an opaque type by external code while remaining fully defined within its defining module.

rules.title: Struct construction uses the form Type { field = expression, ... } . Field names identify the destination fiel
rules.summary: Struct construction uses the form Type { field = expression, ... } . Field names identify the destination fields, and each field MUST be initialized exactly once.

It is not an ordinary associated function and MUST NOT be invoked explicitly as part of normal source-language execution.

rules.title: The hook receives exclusive mutable access to the owned value while destruction is performed and MAY release r
rules.summary: The hook receives exclusive mutable access to the owned value while destruction is performed and MAY release resources managed directly by T that are not represented by owned fields.

rules.title: The hook MUST NOT independently destroy owned fields that the implementation will subsequently destroy
rules.summary: The hook MUST NOT independently destroy owned fields that the implementation will subsequently destroy.

rules.title: After the destruction hook completes, the implementation recursively destroys the remaining owned fields accor
rules.summary: After the destruction hook completes, the implementation recursively destroys the remaining owned fields according to their destruction semantics.

rules.title: The destruction hook MUST return void and MUST NOT be invoked explicitly by ordinary program code
rules.summary: The destruction hook MUST return void and MUST NOT be invoked explicitly by ordinary program code.

rules.title: It is a destruction hook rather than an ordinary callable function. The implementation invokes it exactly once
rules.summary: It is a destruction hook rather than an ordinary callable function. The implementation invokes it exactly once for each owned value whose type defines one.

rules.summary: Variant names MUST be unique within the enum. Variants are part of the enum's semantic interface and MAY be used to construct and pattern-match values.

rules.summary: An enum MAY have zero variants. Such an enum has no constructible value and therefore can only be used in contexts that do not require producing a value.

rules.title: The number and types of initializer elements MUST match the array type
rules.summary: The number and types of initializer elements MUST match the array type.

rules.title: Safe indexing MUST remain within the valid range
rules.summary: Safe indexing MUST remain within the valid range.

rules.summary: A non- void function MUST return a value compatible with its declared return type on every successful control-flow path.

rules.title: A void function MUST NOT return a value
rules.summary: A void function MUST NOT return a value.

rules.summary: An associated function is otherwise an ordinary function. All parameters MUST be declared explicitly, and association does not alter the function's parameter list, calling convention, ownership, borrowing, mutability, lifetime, or return-value semantics.

A mutable parameter therefore MUST be declared with the mut qualifier on the managed-pointer type when the function is intended to modify the referenced value.

rules.summary: The :: qualification syntax determines whether associated-function lookup is performed. It does not alter the function's declared parameter list or introduce an implicit receiver. The . operator remains member access and MUST NOT introduce implicit method lookup or invocation.

rules.location: 24. Functions — Associated Function Identity and Name Resolution [L722-L859]
rules.summary: Likewise, the existence of an associated function MUST NOT cause it to be selected by an unqualified call.

rules.location: 24. Functions — Associated Function Identity and Name Resolution [L722-L859]
rules.summary: Once an associated function has been selected, the number and types of the explicitly supplied arguments MUST satisfy that function's signature.

rules.summary: Ordinary function-call rules, including evaluation order, ownership, borrowing, mutability, lifetime, and type compatibility, then apply.

rules.summary: A module MAY export types and functions through its export { ... } block to form its external interface.

rules.summary: For integers, an operation whose mathematical result is outside the destination type's range is an arithmetic failure. Such an operation MUST NOT silently wrap, produce an unspecified value, or otherwise produce a value that is treated as a successful result in safe code.

rules.summary: An arithmetic failure that can be determined at compile time MUST be diagnosed as a compile-time error.

rules.title: The implementation MUST NOT generate code that evaluates such an operation as a successful operation
rules.summary: The implementation MUST NOT generate code that evaluates such an operation as a successful operation.

rules.title: An arithmetic failure that cannot be determined at compile time MUST be detected when the operation is evaluat
rules.summary: An arithmetic failure that cannot be determined at compile time MUST be detected when the operation is evaluated at runtime.

rules.title: A runtime arithmetic failure MUST NOT produce a value, and execution MUST NOT continue past the failed operati
rules.summary: A runtime arithmetic failure MUST NOT produce a value, and execution MUST NOT continue past the failed operation as though it had successfully completed.

rules.title: The mechanism used to report a runtime arithmetic failure is implementation-defined. An implementation MAY use
rules.summary: The mechanism used to report a runtime arithmetic failure is implementation-defined. An implementation MAY use a checked error, a runtime trap, program termination, or another documented failure mechanism, provided that the mechanism preserves the guarantees of safe code.
ambiguities: Exact behavior is implementation-defined to the extent permitted by the cited rule/profile.

rules.title: The implementation MUST document the mechanism it uses
rules.summary: The implementation MUST document the mechanism it uses.

rules.title: The implementation-defined reporting mechanism MUST NOT change whether the operation is considered to have fai
rules.summary: The implementation-defined reporting mechanism MUST NOT change whether the operation is considered to have failed.
ambiguities: Exact behavior is implementation-defined to the extent permitted by the cited rule/profile.

rules.summary: Portable programs MUST NOT depend on a particular reporting mechanism, but MAY rely on the guarantees that a failed arithmetic operation produces no value, does not silently succeed, and does not result in undefined memory behavior.

rules.title: Floating-point operations follow the implementation's documented floating-point model. The model MUST define t
rules.summary: Floating-point operations follow the implementation's documented floating-point model. The model MUST define the behavior of infinities and NaNs if the implementation exposes them.

rules.title: For floating-point values, equality follows the implementation's documented floating-point model. If NaN value
rules.summary: For floating-point values, equality follows the implementation's documented floating-point model. If NaN values are supported, implementations MUST document whether NaN compares equal to itself; the default CobaltC rule is that NaN is not equal to any value, including itself.

rules.title: Assignment MUST preserve the ownership, initialization, lifetime, borrowing, and destruction invariants applic
rules.summary: Assignment MUST preserve the ownership, initialization, lifetime, borrowing, and destruction invariants applicable to both the destination and the resulting value.

rules.title: An assignment MUST NOT create an additional owner, invalidate a live borrow without an applicable invalidation
rules.summary: An assignment MUST NOT create an additional owner, invalidate a live borrow without an applicable invalidation rule, or cause a value to be destroyed more than once.

rules.title: Once a non-copyable argument is moved into a parameter, the caller no longer owns it. Borrowed parameters do n
rules.summary: Once a non-copyable argument is moved into a parameter, the caller no longer owns it. Borrowed parameters do not transfer ownership. A function that wants to return ownership to its caller MUST return the value explicitly as part of its result.

rules.title: The condition MUST have type bool . An else if chain is equivalent to nested conditionals
rules.summary: The condition MUST have type bool . An else if chain is equivalent to nested conditionals.

rules.title: Match arms are evaluated in source order and the first matching arm is selected. The _ pattern matches any val
rules.summary: Match arms are evaluated in source order and the first matching arm is selected. The _ pattern matches any value not matched by an earlier arm. The compiler MUST reject statically non-exhaustive matches over a finite set of known variants or otherwise exhaustively enumerable cases.

rules.title: Returning an owned value transfers ownership to the caller. Returning a managed pointer is permitted only when
rules.summary: Returning an owned value transfers ownership to the caller. Returning a managed pointer is permitted only when its lifetime remains valid after the function returns. A managed pointer to an ordinary local variable MUST NOT be returned.

rules.title: A deferred block observes the current value of each referenced binding or subobject at the time the deferred b
rules.summary: A deferred block observes the current value of each referenced binding or subobject at the time the deferred block executes. Registering a deferred block therefore creates a future use of each referenced binding or subobject path. The referenced binding or subobject path MUST remain valid until the deferred block has executed and MUST be initialized when the deferred block executes.

rules.title: The value held by a referenced binding or subobject MAY be replaced, reassigned, or otherwise changed before d
rules.summary: The value held by a referenced binding or subobject MAY be replaced, reassigned, or otherwise changed before deferred execution when permitted by the ordinary ownership, initialization, borrowing, lifetime, and destruction rules.

rules.title: Such an operation changes the value observed by the deferred block; it does not remove the deferred reference
rules.summary: Such an operation changes the value observed by the deferred block; it does not remove the deferred reference to the binding or subobject path.

rules.title: A value instance held by a binding or subobject referenced by a deferred block MUST NOT be moved out of, destr
rules.summary: A value instance held by a binding or subobject referenced by a deferred block MUST NOT be moved out of, destroyed, or otherwise invalidated in a manner that leaves the referenced binding or subobject path uninitialized or invalid when the deferred block executes.

rules.title: A move that leaves the referenced path moved-from is therefore prohibited unless that path is reinitialized be
rules.summary: A move that leaves the referenced path moved-from is therefore prohibited unless that path is reinitialized before deferred execution.

rules.title: A deferred reference to a binding does not by itself require every subobject of that binding to remain initial
rules.summary: A deferred reference to a binding does not by itself require every subobject of that binding to remain initialized. If a deferred block references only a particular field or subobject, disjoint fields or subobjects MAY be moved or otherwise modified when permitted by the partial-move, borrowing, and lifetime rules.

rules.title: The specifically referenced path MUST remain valid and MUST be initialized when the deferred block executes
rules.summary: The specifically referenced path MUST remain valid and MUST be initialized when the deferred block executes.

rules.title: Deferred blocks execute before the destruction of owned locals in their associated scope. Consequently, a defe
rules.summary: Deferred blocks execute before the destruction of owned locals in their associated scope. Consequently, a deferred block MAY access an owned local that would otherwise be destroyed when the scope is exited.

rules.title: A deferred block MUST NOT access a binding or subobject whose lifetime ends before the deferred block executes
rules.summary: A deferred block MUST NOT access a binding or subobject whose lifetime ends before the deferred block executes.

rules.title: If such access would occur, the program is ill-formed
rules.summary: If such access would occur, the program is ill-formed.

rules.title: If execution of a deferred block itself transfers ownership, destroys a value, moves a field, or otherwise cha
rules.summary: If execution of a deferred block itself transfers ownership, destroys a value, moves a field, or otherwise changes the initialization or ownership state of a referenced path, the resulting state MUST be respected by subsequent deferred blocks and by automatic scope destruction.

rules.title: A value or subobject MUST NOT be destroyed more than once
rules.summary: A value or subobject MUST NOT be destroyed more than once.

rules.title: A value MUST be initialized before it is read
rules.summary: A value MUST be initialized before it is read.

rules.summary: The compiler MUST perform control-flow-sensitive definite-initialization analysis sufficient to establish whether every path reaching a read has initialized the value.

rules.title: Managed pointers are non-owning. Library abstractions MAY implement shared ownership, but such ownership MUST
rules.summary: Managed pointers are non-owning. Library abstractions MAY implement shared ownership, but such ownership MUST be explicit in the abstraction and is not inferred from an ordinary managed pointer.

rules.title: Shared ownership implemented by a library is an abstraction-level resource-management mechanism, not an additi
rules.summary: Shared ownership implemented by a library is an abstraction-level resource-management mechanism, not an additional ordinary ownership state of the language.

rules.title: A value is copyable only when its type's copy contract permits copying. The predefined value types and shared
rules.summary: A value is copyable only when its type's copy contract permits copying. The predefined value types and shared managed pointers are copyable unless otherwise stated. A user-defined aggregate is copyable when all of its owned components are copyable and the type does not define a destruction hook. Types provided by the standard library MAY define their own copy contracts.

rules.title: A mutable managed pointer is not copyable. A copy operation produces an independent value according to the typ
rules.summary: A mutable managed pointer is not copyable. A copy operation produces an independent value according to the type's copy contract.

rules.title: After the move, a remains a binding but no longer owns the transferred value. It MUST NOT be read, moved, or d
rules.summary: After the move, a remains a binding but no longer owns the transferred value. It MUST NOT be read, moved, or destroyed as though it still owned that value.

rules.title: The moved-from binding may be reassigned with a newly initialized value
rules.summary: The moved-from binding may be reassigned with a newly initialized value.

rules.title: For aggregate values, an individual owned component MAY be moved independently when the resulting ownership st
rules.summary: For aggregate values, an individual owned component MAY be moved independently when the resulting ownership state is well-defined according to the language rules.

rules.title: After a component is moved, that component is considered moved from the containing aggregate. The containing a
rules.summary: After a component is moved, that component is considered moved from the containing aggregate. The containing aggregate remains usable through components that remain owned and initialized. A moved component MUST NOT subsequently be accessed through its original ownership path until it is reinitialized.

rules.title: An aggregate MUST NOT be used in an operation that requires ownership or initialization of a moved component
rules.summary: An aggregate MUST NOT be used in an operation that requires ownership or initialization of a moved component.

rules.title: In particular, an aggregate with a moved component MUST NOT be moved, copied, returned, or passed by value whe
rules.summary: In particular, an aggregate with a moved component MUST NOT be moved, copied, returned, or passed by value when doing so would require that component to be available.

rules.title: A moved component MUST NOT be destroyed again through the original aggregate ownership path
rules.summary: A moved component MUST NOT be destroyed again through the original aggregate ownership path.

rules.title: If the aggregate later reaches destruction, only the components that remain owned and initialized by that aggr
rules.summary: If the aggregate later reaches destruction, only the components that remain owned and initialized by that aggregate are destroyed.

rules.title: A moved component MAY be reinitialized through its original ownership path when the language rules permit assi
rules.summary: A moved component MAY be reinitialized through its original ownership path when the language rules permit assignment to an uninitialized component.

rules.title: Once reinitialized, the component is again owned and initialized by the containing aggregate and participates
